title: AI Versus The Labor Market

AI Versus The Labor Market

Tan Kai Xian

Gavekal Research | 3 Sep 2026

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has long argued that the massive artificial-intelligence capital spending boom in the US will improve labor productivity. Like the technology boom of the late 1990s, he expects this technological transformation to support real GDP growth and weigh on inflation. So far, however, solid US productivity growth since the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022 has coincided with rising inflation and real GDP growth continuing to chug along at around its 20-year median of 2.3% (see chart below). The missing piece in the puzzle may be the labor market. AI is helping workers produce more, but a shortage of workers is constraining the economy’s ability to increase supply fast enough to meet the additional demand generated by the compute build-out.
